message.","fact_ids":["sec06-R11","sec06-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on sign colors. The manual says that knowing the signs is needed to get an Indiana driver's license, and it says seven background colors are commonly used on signs. Indiana traffic signs are put up by the Indiana Department of Transportation and local governments, and they rely on colors, shapes, written messages and symbols so drivers can grasp them quickly. In this lesson you will match each background color to the kind of message it carries, and then sort out the two pairs of colors that are easiest to mix up.","fact_ids":["sec06-R11","sec06-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Brown, blue and green","fact_ids":["sec06-F02","sec06-F03","sec06-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Brown: recreational or cultural sites.","fact_ids":["sec06-F02","sec06-F03","sec06-F04"]},{"text":"Blue: road services and information.","fact_ids":["sec06-F02","sec06-F03","sec06-F04"]},{"text":"Green: movements, directions, guidance.","fact_ids":["sec06-F02","sec06-F03","sec06-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Start with three colors that guide and inform. A brown sign points to a nearby recreational or cultural site, such as a state park. A blue sign gives road services and information, such as the amenities at an upcoming exit. A green sign shows permitted movements, directions or guidance, such as highway entrances and exits, or the distance to destinations ahead. So brown is for recreation and culture, blue is for services, and green is for guidance. None of these three colors is the color for a warning or for a rule you must obey.","fact_ids":["sec06-F02","sec06-F03","sec06-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Orange and white","fact_ids":["sec06-F05","sec06-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Orange: temporary conditions, usually work ahead.","fact_ids":["sec06-F05","sec06-F06"]},{"text":"White: regulations and helpful information.","fact_ids":["sec06-F05","sec06-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Next, orange and white. An orange sign warns of temporary traffic conditions, most often from highway construction or maintenance work ahead. A white sign shows regulations a driver must obey, such as speed limits, and it also carries helpful information like state highway markers. So when you see orange, think of something temporary on the road ahead, such as a work zone. When you see white, think of a rule you must follow or of information such as a route marker. A speed limit is an example the manual gives for a white sign.","fact_ids":["sec06-F05","sec06-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Yellow, yellow-green and red","fact_ids":["sec06-F07","sec06-F08","sec06-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Yellow: conditions and hazards ahead.","fact_ids":["sec06-F07","sec06-F08","sec06-F09"]},{"text":"Yellow-green: schools, pedestrians, bicycles.","fact_ids":["sec06-F07","sec06-F08","sec06-F09"]},{"text":"Red: immediate action.","fact_ids":["sec06-F07","sec06-F08","sec06-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Three colors remain. A yellow sign prepares drivers for specific road conditions and hazards ahead and can alert them to a nearby school zone. A fluorescent yellow-green sign warns of nearby schools, pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds and school bus routes. A red sign carries a regulation that demands immediate action to avoid a safety threat, and the manual gives the Wrong Way sign as an example. So yellow and fluorescent yellow-green both warn, with yellow-green focused on schools and people on foot or on bicycles, while red tells you to act right away.","fact_ids":["sec06-F07","sec06-F08","sec06-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Two color pairs","fact_ids":["sec06-R01","sec06-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Yellow versus yellow-green.","fact_ids":["sec06-R01","sec06-R02"]},{"text":"Orange versus red.","fact_ids":["sec06-R01","sec06-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Two pairs of colors are easy to confuse. Plain yellow signs cover road conditions and hazards in general, while fluorescent yellow-green signs focus on schools, pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds and school bus routes. The second pair is orange and red. Orange signs flag temporary conditions such as work zones, whereas red signs carry regulations that require immediate action. When a question describes a color, decide first whether it is a general warning, a school-related warning, a temporary condition or an immediate-action rule, and the right answer follows.","fact_ids":["sec06-R01","sec06-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check a color","fact_ids":["sec06-F09","sec06-R02","sec06-F05","sec06-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"A regulation demanding immediate action.","fact_ids":["sec06-F09","sec06-R02","sec06-F05","sec06-F06"]},{"text":"Which color?","fact_ids":["sec06-F09","sec06-R02","sec06-F05","sec06-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: which background color does the manual give a sign that carries a regulation demanding immediate action, such as the Wrong Way sign? Go through the colors you just learned. Orange flags temporary conditions such as work zones, white shows regulations such as speed limits, and yellow warns of hazards ahead. The color for a regulation that demands immediate action to avoid a safety threat is red. So the answer is red. If you chose orange, remember that orange is for temporary conditions, while red is for acting right away.","fact_ids":["sec06-F09","sec06-R02","sec06-F05","sec06-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Colors in one look","fact_ids":["sec06-F02","sec06-F03","sec06-F04","sec06-F05","sec06-F06","sec06-F07","sec06-F08","sec06-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Brown, blue, green guide and inform.","fact_ids":["sec06-F02","sec06-F03","sec06-F04","sec06-F05","sec06-F06","sec06-F07","sec06-F08","sec06-F09"]},{"text":"Orange, yellow, yellow-green warn.","fact_ids":["sec06-F02","sec06-F03","sec06-F04","sec06-F05","sec06-F06","sec06-F07","sec06-F08","sec06-F09"]},{"text":"White and red set rules.","fact_ids":["sec06-F02","sec06-F03","sec06-F04","sec06-F05","sec06-F06","sec06-F07","sec06-F08","sec06-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us wrap up. Brown points to recreational or cultural sites, blue gives road services and information, and green shows movements, directions and guidance. Orange warns of temporary conditions such as work ahead. White shows regulations such as speed limits and helpful information such as state highway markers. Yellow prepares you for road conditions and hazards and can alert you to a school zone, fluorescent yellow-green warns of schools, pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds and school bus routes, and red carries a regulation that demands immediate message.","fact_ids":["sec06-R12","sec06-R03","sec06-R04","sec06-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on sign shapes. The manual lists seven common sign shapes, and each one points to a type of message. In this lesson you will learn what a circle, a triangle, a pennant, a rectangle, a diamond, a pentagon and an octagon each tell you. You will also sort out the shape pairs that the manual sets side by side: the three-sided sign versus the eight-sided sign, the diamond versus the rectangle, and the round sign versus the five-sided sign. By the end you will be able to name the message of each of the seven shapes.","fact_ids":["sec06-R12","sec06-R03","sec06-R04","sec06-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Circle, triangle, octagon","fact_ids":["sec06-F10","sec06-F11","sec06-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Circle: railroad crossing ahead.","fact_ids":["sec06-F10","sec06-F11","sec06-F16"]},{"text":"Triangle: slow and be ready to yield.","fact_ids":["sec06-F10","sec06-F11","sec06-F16"]},{"text":"Octagon: stop and yield right of way.","fact_ids":["sec06-F10","sec06-F11","sec06-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"A circular sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up. A triangle sign with three equal sides tells drivers to slow down near an intersection and be ready to stop fully to yield to other drivers or pedestrians. An eight-sided sign tells drivers they must stop and yield the proper right of way at the intersection. So the circle is a warning about a railroad crossing, while the triangle and the octagon both deal with right of way. The difference is that the triangle asks you to be ready to stop, and the octagon tells you that you must stop.","fact_ids":["sec06-F10","sec06-F11","sec06-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Pennant, rectangle, diamond, pentagon","fact_ids":["sec06-F12","sec06-F13","sec06-F14","sec06-F15","sec06-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Pennant: no passing on the left.","fact_ids":["sec06-F12","sec06-F13","sec06-F14","sec06-F15","sec06-R04"]},{"text":"Rectangle: rule, information or warning.","fact_ids":["sec06-F12","sec06-F13","sec06-F14","sec06-F15","sec06-R04"]},{"text":"Diamond: hazards; pentagon: school area.","fact_ids":["sec06-F12","sec06-F13","sec06-F14","sec06-F15","sec06-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"A pennant-shaped sign is posted on the left side of a two-way road to warn drivers not to pass vehicles on the left. A rectangular sign can show a regulation such as a speed limit, helpful information such as a route marker, or a hazard warning such as an advisory speed for a sharp curve. A diamond-shaped sign warns of road conditions and hazards ahead, such as a road that is slippery when wet. A five-sided sign warns that you are entering an area near a school where children may be crossing. The manual adds that an advisory curve speed is often paired with a diamond sign.","fact_ids":["sec06-F12","sec06-F13","sec06-F14","sec06-F15","sec06-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Shape pairs to keep apart","fact_ids":["sec06-R03","sec06-R05","sec06-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Triangle yields; octagon stops.","fact_ids":["sec06-R03","sec06-R05","sec06-R04"]},{"text":"Circle rails; pentagon school.","fact_ids":["sec06-R03","sec06-R05","sec06-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. A three-sided sign asks you to slow and be ready to stop in order to yield, but an eight-sided sign requires you to stop. A round sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead, whereas a five-sided sign warns of a school area. A third pair is the diamond and the rectangle. A diamond sign is a hazard warning, while a rectangular sign may be a regulation, information or a warning such as an advisory curve speed. When a question names a shape, recall which pair it belongs to, and then pick the meaning that goes with that exact shape.","fact_ids":["sec06-R03","sec06-R05","sec06-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check a shape","fact_ids":["sec06-F15","sec06-R05","sec06-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Children may be crossing.","fact_ids":["sec06-F15","sec06-R05","sec06-F10"]},{"text":"Which shape?","fact_ids":["sec06-F15","sec06-R05","sec06-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: which sign shape warns that you are entering an area near a school where children may be crossing? Look back at the shapes. A circle warns of a railroad crossing, a triangle tells you to slow and be ready to yield, a diamond warns of hazards ahead, and an octagon tells you to stop. The shape for a school area where children may be crossing is the five-sided sign. So the answer is the five-sided sign. If you chose the circle, remember that a round sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. The five-sided sign is the school-area shape.","fact_ids":["sec06-F15","sec06-R05","sec06-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Shapes in one look","fact_ids":["sec06-R12","sec06-F10","sec06-F11","sec06-F16","sec06-F12","sec06-F13","sec06-F14","sec06-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Eight stop, three yield.","fact_ids":["sec06-R12","sec06-F10","sec06-F11","sec06-F16","sec06-F12","sec06-F13","sec06-F14","sec06-F15"]},{"text":"Five school, round railroad.","fact_ids":["sec06-R12","sec06-F10","sec06-F11","sec06-F16","sec06-F12","sec06-F13","sec06-F14","sec06-F15"]},{"text":"Pennant no passing, diamond hazards.","fact_ids":["sec06-R12","sec06-F10","sec06-F11","sec06-F16","sec06-F12","sec06-F13","sec06-F14","sec06-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us wrap up. The manual lists seven common shapes. A circle warns of a railroad crossing ahead. A three-sided triangle means slow down and be ready to stop to yield, and an eight-sided sign means stop and yield the proper right of way. A pennant on the left side of a two-way road warns against passing. A rectangle can show a regulation, helpful information or a hazard warning such as an advisory curve speed. A diamond warns of road conditions and hazards ahead, and a five-sided sign warns of an area near a school where children may be crossing.","fact_ids":["sec06-R12","sec06-F10","sec06-F11","sec06-F16","sec06-F12","sec06-F13","sec06-F14","sec06-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec06-u03","module_id":"sec06-m03","objective_ids":["sec06-u03"],"title":{"text":"Families of signs","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Signs fall into families, such as warning, construction, regulation, guidance and services signs, each with its own job.","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15","sec06-R17","sec06-R18"]},{"text":"The slow-moving vehicle emblem marks a vehicle that cannot go faster than twenty-five miles per hour.","fact_ids":["sec06-F17"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"A driver sees a plaque mounted under a stop sign.","fact_ids":["sec06-R16"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A supplemental plaque under a stop sign shows which directions at that intersection must stop.","fact_ids":["sec06-R16"]},"result":{"text":"The driver reads the plaque to learn which directions at the intersection must stop.","fact_ids":["sec06-R16"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking orange construction signs only ever warn of work zones.","fact_ids":["sec06-R14"]},"correction":{"text":"Orange construction signs mainly warn of work zones, but some give guidance such as detours or state rules such as added penalties in a worksite.","fact_ids":["sec06-R14"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Warn, build, rule, guide, serve, and the orange slow emblem.","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15","sec06-R17","sec06-R18","sec06-F17"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A plaque is mounted beneath a stop sign. What information does it give?","fact_ids":["sec06-R16"]},"answer":{"text":"Which directions at that intersection must stop.","fact_ids":["sec06-R16"]},"rationale":{"text":"The plaque is added under a stop sign to show which directions at the intersection must stop.","fact_ids":["sec06-R16"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec06-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Signs come in families","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15","sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18","sec06-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Warning, construction, regulation.","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15","sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18","sec06-F17"]},{"text":"Guidance and services.","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15","sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18","sec06-F17"]},{"text":"One emblem for slow vehicles.","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15","sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18","sec06-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on families of signs. Besides color and shape, the manual groups signs by the job they do. In this lesson you will learn what warning signs do as a family, what orange construction signs can show, what traffic regulation signs and speed advisory signs do, what a supplemental plaque under a stop sign tells you, what guidance signs and driver services signs tell drivers, and what the slow-moving vehicle emblem looks like and marks. Each family has one main job, and knowing it helps you read a sign quickly.","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15","sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18","sec06-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Warnings, work zones and rules","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Warning signs prepare drivers.","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15"]},{"text":"Construction signs: work zones, detours, penalties.","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15"]},{"text":"Regulation signs and advisory speeds.","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15"]}],"narration":{"text":"Warning signs as a family prepare drivers for road conditions and hazards ahead. Orange construction signs mainly warn of work zones, but some give guidance such as detours, or state rules such as added penalties in a worksite. Traffic regulation signs control speed and movement and show rules drivers must obey. Speed advisory signs may be mounted with some warning signs. So a warning sign prepares you, a construction sign usually warns of a work zone but can also guide or state a rule, and a regulation sign tells you the rule you must obey.","fact_ids":["sec06-R13","sec06-R14","sec06-R15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Plaques, guidance, services, emblem","fact_ids":["sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18","sec06-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Stop plaque: which directions stop.","fact_ids":["sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18","sec06-F17"]},{"text":"Guidance and services signs.","fact_ids":["sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18","sec06-F17"]},{"text":"Slow-moving emblem: twenty-five maximum.","fact_ids":["sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18","sec06-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"A supplemental plaque under a stop sign shows which directions at that intersection must stop. Traffic guidance signs tell drivers the type of road, upcoming entrances and exits, and distances to destinations. Driver services and recreation signs tell drivers about nearby amenities, parks and recreation areas. The slow-moving vehicle emblem has a fluorescent orange center and red reflective borders, and it marks a vehicle that cannot go faster than twenty-five miles per hour. Those four items finish the families covered in this lesson.","fact_ids":["sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18","sec06-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":33,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Construction signs do more","fact_ids":["sec06-R14","sec06-R16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: orange only means work ahead.","fact_ids":["sec06-R14","sec06-R16"]},{"text":"Some guide; some state rules.","fact_ids":["sec06-R14","sec06-R16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Because orange signs warn of temporary conditions, it is easy to think every orange construction sign is just a warning. The manual says orange construction signs mainly warn of work zones, but some give guidance, such as detours, and some state rules, such as added penalties in a worksite. A second point to keep straight is the stop sign plaque. A supplemental plaque under a stop sign does not change the sign's color or shape; it shows which directions at that intersection must stop. Read the extra plaque or panel before you decide what to do.","fact_ids":["sec06-R14","sec06-R16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec06-u03-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check a stop plaque","fact_ids":["sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18"]},"lines":[{"text":"Plaque under a stop sign.","fact_ids":["sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18"]},{"text":"What does it show?","fact_ids":["sec06-R16","sec06-R17","sec06-R18"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: what does a supplemental plaque mounted under a stop sign show? Think about the families you just covered. Guidance signs show road types, exits and distances, and services signs show amenities, parks and recreation areas.
